apollos.title: Apollos
apollos.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
apollos.note: An eloquent Jewish preacher from Alexandria who knew the Scriptures and taught accurately about Jesus, though he knew only John's baptism. Priscilla and Aquila took him aside and explained the way of God more fully. In Corinth he did so well that a faction started claiming him over Paul.

artemas.title: Artemas
artemas.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
artemas.note: Paul thought of sending him to Crete to take over from Titus. Later church tradition makes him bishop of Lystra, though the New Testament does not say so.

christ.title: Christ
christ.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
christ.note: A title, not a surname. It is the Greek for the Hebrew Messiah, the anointed one, and the New Testament gives it to Jesus of Nazareth as the king, priest and deliverer the Old Testament promised. His life and ministry are under Jesus.

cretan.title: Cretan
cretan.note: People of Crete, the big island where Paul left Titus to set the churches in order and appoint elders.

crete.title: Crete
crete.note: Paul left Titus here to organise the churches and appoint elders. His ship also put in at the island on the storm voyage to Rome.

jesus.title: Jesus
jesus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
jesus.note: Born in Bethlehem to Mary and raised in Nazareth in Galilee. Around thirty he began teaching in parables, healing, and gathering twelve disciples, until he was arrested in Jerusalem at Passover, tried before the council and Pontius Pilate, and crucified. His followers said he rose bodily three days later, and the New Testament names him the Messiah, God's own Son become human.

jewish.title: Jewish
jewish.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
jewish.note: Not a person. Paul tells Titus that believers on Crete should not give their attention to "Jewish fables", which probably means legends spun around Old Testament figures and genealogies, not the Hebrew Scriptures themselves.

nicopolis.title: Nicopolis
nicopolis.note: Paul wanted Titus to come and spend the winter with him here (Titus 3:12). The name means city of victory, and the likeliest candidate is the one in Epirus, on Greece's northwestern coast.

paul.title: Paul
paul.about: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
paul.note: Born Saul, a Jew of the tribe of Benjamin and a Roman citizen from Tarsus. He trained as a Pharisee under Gamaliel and hunted the early church. Then the risen Christ met him in a blinding vision.

titus.title: Titus
titus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
titus.note: A Gentile convert who worked with Paul. He carried a hard letter to the church at Corinth and brought back word of how it landed. Paul later left him in Crete to organize the churches, and the letter to Titus is the instructions.

tychicus.title: Tychicus
tychicus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
tychicus.note: He carried Paul's letters, Ephesians and Colossians among them, and told the churches in person how Paul was doing.

zenas.title: Zenas
zenas.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
zenas.note: Zenas the lawyer. Paul asks Titus to see him and Apollos off well supplied. Whether he knew Jewish or Roman law is uncertain.
